full_text_en:
Zhengzhou Yetou Network Technology Co., Ltd. v. Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd., Ding Xiaomei, et al. — Pre-execution Restoration of Sales Link in Design Patent Infringement Dispute

**Case Summary**

Where a right holder complains to an e-commerce platform that a seller on the platform infringes its intellectual property rights, and the e-commerce platform removes the sales link of the relevant product in accordance with the relevant provisions of the E-commerce Law, the seller may apply to the court for a ruling requiring the e-commerce platform to pre-execute the restoration of the removed sales link. The people's court shall comprehensively consider factors such as the likelihood of infringement by the sold product, whether the removal of the sales link may cause irreparable damage to the seller, the guarantee provided by the seller, and whether the removal or restoration of the link is detrimental to social public interests, and decide whether to pre-execute the restoration of the removed sales link.

**Applicant**: Zhengzhou Yetou Network Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Guancheng District, Zhengzhou, Henan Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Xiaolong, Executive Director of the Company.

**Respondent**: Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd., domiciled at Yuhang District, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province.
Legal Representative: Jiang Fan, Chairman of the Company.

**Respondent**: Ding Xiaomei, female, born on February 3, 1980, Han nationality, domiciled in Tongzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

**Respondent**: Nantong Su'ao Textile Co., Ltd., domiciled at High-tech Zone, Nantong City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Xiaolong, Executive Director of the Company.

Ding Xiaomei filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province regarding a dispute over infringement of design patent with Zhengzhou Yetou Network Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Yetou Company"), Nantong Su'ao Textile Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Su'ao Company"), and Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Tmall Company"). During the trial, Yetou Company, as applicant, applied to the court on June 10, 2019 for a ruling to pre-execute the restoration of the removed sales link.

Applicant Yetou Company applied for an order requiring Respondent Tmall Company to pre-execute the restoration of the removed sales link on the following grounds: 1. Yetou Company believed that the accused infringing product did not fall within the scope of protection of the involved design patent. The similarities between the accused infringing product and the involved design lay in the overall shape of the foldable frame of the mosquito net, while the differences lay in the shape and pattern of the mosquito net fabric; among these, the similarities constituted prior design, and the differences could be regarded as the design features of the involved design, i.e., the accused infringing product did not use the design features of the involved patent. Therefore, Yetou Company's acts of manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product did not constitute infringement. 2. Due to the complaint by Respondent Ding Xiaomei, Tmall Company removed the sales link of the accused infringing product, causing irreparable losses to Yetou Company. The accused infringing product was a mosquito net, a seasonal product for summer, and was currently in the peak selling season. Before the removal of the sales link, the product had reached the top position among similar products. The upcoming "June 18" promotion was the second large-scale summer sales promotion event after "Double 11," and the removal of the sales link severely impacted Yetou Company's product sales. Moreover, the trial proceedings in this case would take a certain period of time according to law, and failure to restore the link promptly would cause immeasurable losses to Yetou Company's production and operations. Therefore, to avoid irreparable losses, Yetou Company applied to the court for a ruling requiring Tmall Company to pre-execute the restoration of the sales link of the accused infringing product on the Tmall online shopping platform operated by it.

Respondent Ding Xiaomei argued in defense that, as the holder of the involved design patent, she filed a complaint with Respondent Tmall e-commerce platform against Applicant Yetou Company and others for patent infringement, and lawfully filed a lawsuit with the court against Yetou Company for design patent infringement. The Tmall e-commerce platform should, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the E-commerce Law, remove the sales link of Yetou Company's infringing product. Therefore, Yetou Company's application lacked factual and legal basis and should be rejected.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province found the following facts upon trial:

On January 28, 2016, Respondent Ding Xiaomei applied to the National Intellectual Property Administration for a design patent entitled "Portable Folding Mosquito Net for Infants and Young Children," which was granted on June 22, 2016. On the same day, Ding Xiaomei applied for a utility model patent for "A Portable Folding Mosquito Net for Infants and Young Children," which was granted but subsequently declared invalid in March 2017.

Applicant Yetou Company was the operator of the Taobao store "Tongmeng Maternal and Infant Flagship Store," and Respondent Su'ao Company was an affiliated company of Yetou Company. On March 2, 2019, Respondent Ding Xiaomei filed a complaint with Respondent Tmall Company, alleging that the light-blocking U-shaped mosquito net and the upgraded U-shaped mosquito net manufactured and sold by Yetou Company and Su'ao Company, i.e., the accused infringing products, infringed her design patent. On March 7, 2019, Yetou Company submitted a "Counter-Notice," "Appeal Statement for Tmall Intellectual Property Complaint," and relevant comparative documents to Tmall Company, undertaking that the complained light-blocking U-shaped mosquito net and upgraded U-shaped mosquito net displayed on the Tmall platform did not infringe Ding Xiaomei's intellectual property rights. After receiving the complaint, Tmall Company commissioned the Zhejiang Intellectual Property Research and Service Center to conduct patent infringement determinations on March 12, March 20, and April 2, 2019, and the latter issued three "Patent Infringement Determination Consultation Reports," all concluding that patent infringement was not established. Tmall Company therefore did not take measures such as removing the sales link.

On March 26, 2019, Respondent Ding Xiaomei filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province against Applicant Yetou Company, Respondent Su'ao Company, and Tmall Company. On April 4, 2019, Ding Xiaomei submitted a "Counter-Appeal and Litigation Explanation" to Tmall Company, arguing that, on the one hand, Yetou Company and Su'ao Company's manufacture and sale of the involved light-blocking U-shaped mosquito net and upgraded U-shaped mosquito net constituted infringement, and on the other hand, she had already filed a lawsuit for design patent infringement, so the Tmall online shopping platform should immediately take necessary measures such as removal, blocking, disconnection, and termination of transactions and services. On April 8, 2019, Tmall Company removed the sales link of the accused infringing products on the Tmall online shopping platform.

Applicant Yetou Company provided corresponding guarantee for this application.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province held that:

First, Respondent Tmall Company handled the complaint of Respondent Ding Xiaomei in accordance with regulations and law. After receiving Ding Xiaomei's complaint, Tmall Company, on the one hand, heard the opinions of the complaining merchant and the complained merchant, and on the other hand, commissioned a third party through its affiliated company to evaluate whether the infringement could be established. The evaluation opinion held that the accused infringing act did not constitute infringement, so it did not take measures such as removing the sales link. After Ding Xiaomei filed this lawsuit, she complained again, insisting that Tmall Company should take necessary measures such as removing the link. Tmall Company then took the measure of removing the sales link.

Second, the possibility that Applicant Yetou Company's manufacture and sale of the accused infringing product constituted infringement was relatively low. Based on the evidence and arguments submitted by the parties and the comparison of infringement, and taking into account the fact that another utility model patent of Respondent Ding Xiaomei, "Portable Folding Mosquito Net for Infants and Young Children," had been declared invalid, the court preliminarily found that the possibility of patent infringement was relatively low.

Third, failure to restore the sales link might cause irreparable damage to Applicant Yetou Company's production and operations. The sales of the accused infringing product largely depended on the accumulation of goodwill and reputation and the grasp of timing. The product involved had strong seasonality, and the possibility of infringement was relatively low. Therefore, if the removed sales link was not restored in a timely manner, it might cause continuous reduction and loss of the goodwill and reputation accumulated by Yetou Company and its accused infringing product, as well as the loss of business opportunities, resulting in irreparable damage to its production and operations.

Fourth, Applicant Yetou Company provided certain guarantee. Yetou Company calculated an amount based on an appropriate multiple of the previous monthly sales of the accused infringing product multiplied by the approximate months of sales after restoration of the link, and accordingly provided a cash guarantee, undertaking that if infringement was established, the compensation liability it might bear could be satisfied. Respondent Tmall Company also undertook to promptly provide all sales records of the accused infringing product after restoration of the link for use in calculating compensation, etc.

In summary, the application of Applicant Yetou Company complies with the provisions of law. In accordance with Article 106, Item (3) and Article 107 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered a ruling on June 14, 2019:

Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd. shall immediately restore the sales links of the accused infringing products involved in the case, namely "Light-blocking U-shaped Mosquito Net" and "Upgraded U-shaped Mosquito Net," on the Tmall online shopping platform.

This civil ruling took effect immediately upon issuance, and neither the applicant nor the respondents applied for reconsideration.

On October 20, 2019, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered a judgment in the case of Ding Xiaomei v. Zhengzhou Yetou Network Technology Co., Ltd., et al. for design patent infringement: rejecting all of Ding Xiaomei's claims. Thereafter, Ding Xiaomei, dissatisfied, appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court. During the court's trial, Ding Xiaomei applied to withdraw the appeal. On March 19, 2020, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered a ruling: permitting Ding Xiaomei to withdraw the appeal.
